Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee expressed shock on Saturday over a tragic Kolkata stampede in which at least 17 people lost their lives. The Trinamool Congress (TMC) alleged poor crowd management and a lack of police presence after the stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity puja pandal. The TMC, in a post on X, following the tragic incident, wrote, "No police, no civic volunteers, no ambulances, no crowd management! This is what local residents are stating in the wake of the tragic stampede at Chorebagan Puja Pandal." Follow live updates on the Kolkata stampede here . Deep Dive Targeting the ruling BJP and the police, the party said, "@KolkataPolice and the @BJP4Bengal administration must answer for these grave lapses. Public safety cannot be treated so casually. As the death toll rises, who will take responsibility? Will @SuvenduWB accept accountability and resign?" "On the very day @AmitShah arrives, Bengal is confronted with this heartbreaking tragedy. Shameful state of affairs," it added. It said, "@KolkataPolice, WHERE WAS THE SECURITY AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE WHEN PEOPLE NEEDED YOU MOST?" "Eyewitnesses and local residents allege that there was little to no police presence to control the crowd at Chorebagan Puja Pandal. In the aftermath of the stampede, it was ordinary citizens who stepped in to rescue the injured, the party added. It further said, "How many more lives must be put at risk before the @BJP4Bengal administration answers for these failures? Why does public safety take a back seat while VIP arrangements receive priority?" Mamata Banerjee expresses shock Former West Bengal CM Banerjee posted on X wishing a speedy recovery of the injured individuals in the stampede. The TMC chief said, "Deeply shocked and saddened to learn about the stampede at the Chore Bagan Puja Pandal." "I pray to Maa Durga for the speedy recovery of all those injured and for strength and courage for their families during this difficult time," she added. The incident occurred at around 7:40 pm, and the pandal has now been closed to visitors, news agency ANI reported, citing Kolkata Police. "Today at around 7:40 pm, a stampede occurred at the exit gate of Sarada Park (Chor Bagan) Puja Pandal, under Girish Park Police Station, due to heavy crowds of pandal hoppers amid rainfall. The Puja Pandal has now been closed to visitors. Apart from PM Modi, home minister Amit Shah, Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, former Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi also expressed condolences.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah has postponed his programmes in West Bengal scheduled for Sunday in the wake of the stampede. news.full_article_text: Government doctor among 3 arrested as Rajasthan ANTF seizes 3.764 kg of raw MD Rajasthan’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force arrested a government doctor and two others after busting an alleged mephedrone manufacturing unit in Balotra. A government doctor was among three people arrested after Rajasthan’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) busted an alleged mephedrone (MD) manufacturing unit at a house in Balotra district on Saturday. Police seized 3.764 kg of raw MD, chemicals and equipment, ₹ 3.41 lakh in cash and a car. The ANTF team, with assistance from local police, raided the premises in the Siwana police station area after receiving information about an alleged MD manufacturing unit, deputy inspector general of police Abhijeet Singh said. Police identified the three arrested men as prime suspect Suresh Kumar Vishnoi (27), a resident of Mithora; Dr Mukesh Vishnoi (29), and Utkarsh Vishnoi (19), a resident of Modran village in Jalore district. From failed government job aspirant to alleged MD manufacturer Suresh completed his graduation and attempted several government recruitment examinations, including those for patwari, gram sevak, Rajasthan Police, forest guard and police sub-inspector posts, but failed to secure a government job, an ANTF officer said. In 2022, he moved to Bengaluru with a friend and began working in pharmaceutical sales as a medical representative. After working in the field for around two years, he allegedly found the earnings insufficient. Police said Suresh returned to his village in 2024 and came into contact with people involved in drug trafficking. He allegedly began purchasing, selling and supplying MD before deciding to manufacture it himself in pursuit of higher profits. Investigators suspect that he learnt the process of manufacturing MD by watching videos on YouTube and other social media platforms. He allegedly used chemicals and equipment to prepare the drug at his house in Mithora. According to the ANTF, Suresh had called Dr Mukesh Vishnoi and Utkarsh Vishnoi to his house to sell a consignment of MD. The two allegedly arrived in a car. Police suspect that Suresh used Dr Mukesh’s contacts to supply the drug in and around Jalore and Siwana. During questioning, Suresh allegedly disclosed details about supplying MD through his associates and other people involved in drug trafficking. Raw MD, chemicals and equipment seized The ANTF team had received information that Suresh was operating an MD manufacturing unit at his house and in the adjoining premises. After verifying the information, the team conducted a raid with local police. Officers said that the three men were found sitting in a shed outside the house. A search of the house and surrounding premises led to the recovery of raw MD, chemicals and equipment allegedly used to manufacture and dry the drug. All three were arrested, and the seized material was taken into custody. The seized material included 3.764 kg of raw MD, including its packaging, and two packets of powder allegedly used in manufacturing the drug, weighing 888 grams including the plastic bags. Police also seized 800 grams of methylene dichloride (MDC) and 514 grams of a chemical described in the seizure details as isopropyl acid. The equipment recovered from the premises included an electric churning machine, an induction cooktop, a large glass jar, a thermometer and a piece of cloth bearing a substance allegedly used in drying MD. In addition, the team seized ₹ 3,41,700 in cash and a Kia Seltos bearing registration number RJ-19-CT-10351.

A government doctor was among three people arrested after Rajasthan’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) busted an alleged mephedrone (MD) manufacturing unit at a house in Balotra district on Saturday. Police seized 3.764 kg of raw MD, chemicals and equipment, ₹ 3.41 lakh in cash and a car.

The ANTF team, with assistance from local police, raided the premises in the Siwana police station area after receiving information about an alleged MD manufacturing unit, deputy inspector general of police Abhijeet Singh said.

Police identified the three arrested men as prime suspect Suresh Kumar Vishnoi (27), a resident of Mithora; Dr Mukesh Vishnoi (29), and Utkarsh Vishnoi (19), a resident of Modran village in Jalore district.

Police suspect that Suresh used Dr Mukesh’s contacts to supply the drug in and around Jalore and Siwana. Police also seized 800 grams of methylene dichloride (MDC) and 514 grams of a chemical described in the seizure details as isopropyl acid. The equipment recovered from the premises included an electric churning machine, an induction cooktop, a large glass jar, a thermometer and a piece of cloth bearing a substance allegedly used in drying MD. In addition, the team seized ₹ 3,41,700 in cash and a Kia Seltos bearing registration number RJ-19-CT-10351.

news.full_article_text: - Published 17 October 2026, 03:33 BST Brazil's government says deforestation rates in the country's Amazon and savanna regions have fallen to record lows ahead of a presidential election run-off in which the rainforest's future is a key issue. Left-wing President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva, when he assumed office three years ago, pledged to end deforestation by 2030 in the Amazon. It had surged under his right-wing predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro. Lula will face Bolsonaro's son Flavio in the run-off on 25 October, with polls suggesting a neck-and-neck race. Flavio is expected to continue his father's policies if he wins, though he has pledged to fight organised crime in the Amazon. Satellite data shows that in the year to July 2026, the deforestation rate fell by 41.8% in the Amazon - the biggest drop since records began in 1988. The fall in the Cerrado, Brazil's savanna region, was 23.8%. The Amazon rainforest - the world's largest - is a crucial buffer in the global fight against climate change and 60% of it is located in Brazil. Why the Amazon rainforest is so important What in the World podcast Jair Bolsonaro promoted mining in indigenous lands in the Amazon and forest clearances soared at the same time as resources to protect the forest were cut. During Bolsonaro's presidency from 2019 to 2022, the Amazon lost nearly 60% more in forest lands compared to the previous four years, news agency AFP reported, citing official data. Lula reversed his policies and oversaw deforestation rates drop to a six-year low during his first year in office. Lula tightened up environmental monitoring and penalties for illegal logging. "Our goal is to achieve zero illegal deforestation by 2030," he said in a post on X on Friday. Tropical rainforests like the Amazon are home to millions of species. In a healthy state, they absorb vast quantities of planet-warming carbon dioxide, helping to keep the Earth cool. But they have come under increasing pressure from decades of deliberate land clearance for agriculture and logging, as well as climate change, which scientists warn can create conditions for wildfires. Brazil's Environment Minister Joao Paulo Capobianco described the decline in Amazon deforestation as "absolutely stratospheric". It was an "historic achievement" for Brazil, said Marcio Astrini, executive secretary at climate advocacy group Observatorio do Clima. It showed that "with political will, it is possible to curb deforestation and greenhouse gas emissions", Astrini said. news.headline: Supreme Court Directs Centre to Launch Portal for Autism Stem Cell Therapy Patients
news.story_lead: The Supreme Court of India has ordered the Union Government to establish a dedicated online portal within six weeks for patients undergoing stem cell therapy for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). The order mandates the creation of a comprehensive database to track patients, clinics, and medical practitioners while enforcing strict regulatory oversight on unauthorized clinical services.
news.full_article_text:
### Regulatory Mandate for Stem Cell Therapy in ASD

A Supreme Court bench comprising Justices JB Pardiwala and R Mahadevan issued key directions to the Union Government regarding stem cell therapy for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Building upon its January 30, 2026 ruling—which banned stem cell therapy as a routine clinical service and restricted it strictly to approved research and clinical trials—the court directed the government to set up a central online portal within six weeks.

### Portal Registration and Temporary Arrangements

- **Target Beneficiaries**: Patients who began stem cell therapy for ASD on or before January 30, 2026, are required to register on the portal.
- **Data Requirements**: Practitioners, clinics, parents, and caregivers must maintain detailed medical records, practitioner details, intervention courses, and clinical progress on the portal with strict confidentiality safeguards.
- **Temporary Continuity**: Registered patients whose therapy started on or prior to January 30, 2026, will be permitted to continue therapy as a strictly temporary arrangement until a Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) is established. The court emphasized that this does not constitute official approval or recognition of stem cell therapy as an established clinical service.

### Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) Framework

In response to earlier directions, the Centre submitted an affidavit on September 28 disclosing that no applications for clinical trials had been received since January 30. The Centre proposed a multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) funded by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR):

- **Sites**: Two tertiary care facilities—one in North India and one in South India.
- **Timeline**: To be established within six months.
- **Court Observations**: The court noted that the proposed RCT lacked clear eligibility criteria for existing patients and directed the Centre to formulate a monitoring plan for excluded patients. Additionally, the Parents’ Forum for Stem Cells in Autism and Cerebral Palsy was permitted to submit suggestions on the trial design.

### Public Information and Legal Awareness

The court criticized the lack of readily available public information regarding regulatory restrictions, which allowed unauthorized clinics and practitioners to offer stem cell treatments. To address this, the Centre was given six weeks to publish a comprehensive protocol on stem cell use in ASD research and clinical trials. Furthermore, a dedicated section must be added to the Ministry of Health's official website explaining the legal status and regulatory requirements in clear, accessible language. The Union Government must submit a compliance report prior to the next hearing scheduled for December 14.

hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### ऑटिज्म स्टेम सेल थेरेपी के लिए नियामक निर्देश

जस्टिस जेबी पारदीवाला और जस्टिस आर महादेवन की पीठ ने ऑटिज्म स्पेक्ट्रम डिसऑर्डर (ASD) के लिए स्टेम सेल थेरेपी के इस्तेमाल पर केंद्र सरकार को सख्त निर्देश दिए हैं। अपने 30 जनवरी 2026 के आदेश को आगे बढ़ाते हुए, जिसमें सामान्य नैदानिक सेवा के रूप में स्टेम सेल थेरेपी पर रोक लगाई गई थी, अदालत ने छह सप्ताह के भीतर एक समर्पित पोर्टल स्थापित करने का आदेश दिया।

### पोर्टल पंजीकरण और अस्थायी व्यवस्था

- **पात्र मरीज**: 30 जनवरी 2026 को या उससे पहले स्टेम सेल थेरेपी शुरू करने वाले मरीजों का पंजीकरण पोर्टल पर अनिवार्य है।
- **आवश्यक विवरण**: डॉक्टरों, क्लीनिकों, और अभिभावकों को मरीज का मेडिकल रिकॉर्ड और उपचार का विवरण पोर्टल पर दर्ज करना होगा।
- **अस्थायी छूट**: पंजीकृत मरीज केवल एक सख्त अस्थायी व्यवस्था के रूप में तब तक इलाज जारी रख सकते हैं जब तक कि रैंडमाइज्ड कंट्रोल ट्रायल (RCT) स्थापित नहीं हो जाता।

### क्लिनिकल ट्रायल और शोध रूपरेखा

केंद्र सरकार ने 28 सितंबर को दिए हलफनामे में बताया कि 30 जनवरी के बाद क्लिनिकल ट्रायल का कोई आवेदन प्राप्त नहीं हुआ है। केंद्र ने ICMR द्वारा वित्तपोषित एक बहु-केंद्रीकृत ट्रायल का प्रस्ताव रखा है जो उत्तर और दक्षिण भारत के दो अस्पतालों में छह महीने के भीतर शुरू होगा।

### सार्वजनिक जागरूकता और दिशानिर्देश

अदालत ने कहा कि सही जानकारी के अभाव में अवैध क्लीनिक फल-फूल रहे हैं। इसलिए केंद्र को छह सप्ताह के भीतर नियम पुस्तिका जारी करने और स्वास्थ्य मंत्रालय की वेबसाइट पर स्पष्ट सार्वजनिक सूचना डालने का निर्देश दिया गया है। मामले की अगली सुनवाई 14 दिसंबर को होगी।
